summary: The agent implemented nearly all duplicate-class behavior and preserved the tested baseline, but one explicit family-coherence scenario failed: when the family root is unavailable, a duplicate member anchors the family, yet a later unique sibling from another own origin was not recognized as belonging to that anchored family and was loaded instead of rejected.
quick_failure_summary: A later unique sibling bypasses coherence for a family anchored by a duplicate member when the root class is unavailable.

details.reasoning: The implementation activates a family from an own-source duplicate and records only the members discovered at that time. In the failing case, metadata available from the duplicated Siblings$One class identifies the unavailable Siblings root but does not enumerate Siblings$Two. When Siblings$Two is later encountered as a nonduplicate, resolveSelection only checks familiesByMember by exact class name and does not discover its metadata root and match that root to the existing anchor. It therefore selects the only candidate from later-members-origin rather than raising the required anchored-family conflict. The hidden suite passed 47 of 48 new tests, so this is a narrow but substantive missed behavior, not an incomplete implementation.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added broad focused tests but did not include the unavailable-root/later-unique-sibling case. It also adjusted an existing SingleClassesTest registration after a full-suite failure; that change deserves maintenance review, but it is not the cause of the reported hidden-test failure.

justification.issue_description: After an exact duplicate anchors a family while its root is unavailable, later members must be associated with the anchored family through their own InnerClasses or EnclosingMethod metadata even if those members were not discoverable during initial activation. A member available only from another own origin must then fail with family, member, anchor, and alternatives identified.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says: 'When the family root is available, its selected origin anchors the family; otherwise the strategy-selected duplicate does. Load later members from that origin. If an encountered member is available only from another own origin, fail.' It also requires families to be determined transitively from InnerClasses and EnclosingMethod metadata. The repository exposes those metadata attributes, and the reference implementation checks the metadata family root of each selected own class against an existing family anchor. The failing test unavailableFamilyRootUsesDuplicateToAnchorLaterMembers directly exercises the quoted behavior.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the missed later-member behavior is expressly stated in the visible prompt and is implementable using visible metadata APIs. This is not an undocumented hidden-test convention, ambiguity, API knowledge gap, or infrastructure failure.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is large and architecturally demanding but fair and solvable. The prompt explicitly covers origin identity and precedence, byte equality, deferred and cached resolution, invalidation, concurrency, logging, output ownership, transitive metadata families, unavailable roots, and later-member conflicts. The single failing test follows the stated unavailable-root rule rather than adding an undocumented requirement.

evidence: JUnit reports show the baseline test passed and 47 of 48 new tests passed; the sole failure is an ordinary assertion that expected a RuntimeException but received none.
The verifier compiled and ran both Gradle test tasks successfully; the new task failed only after executing the targeted family-coherence test.

The trajectory shows the agent completed its implementation and its own full ./gradlew :test run finished BUILD SUCCESSFUL, so no runtime, dependency, service, or bootstrap failure prevented validation.

The trace encountered a missing rg binary and an over-broad find permission warning early, but the agent immediately used grep/find alternatives and continued; these did not materially block the solution.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier exposed a localized implementation gap in later-member family-root association.
